title: WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour (2020)
why: Canonical global dose floor for aerobic, strength and sedentary time

title: Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition (current guidelines)
why: Canonical US dose targets; links full 2nd edition PDF

title: The Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans (JAMA 2018)
why: Official journal statement of the 2018 US guidelines, full text

title: ACSM Position Stand: Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults (2026)
why: Newest ACSM RT stand; overview of 137 reviews, full text free

title: ACSM Position Stand: Quantity and Quality of Exercise (2011)
why: Still-cited baseline prescription across cardio, RT, flexibility, neuromotor

title: The Resistance Training Dose Response: Meta-Regressions on Weekly Volume and Frequency (Sports Med 2026)
why: Newest volume and frequency dose-response meta-regression; supersedes older volume work

title: Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and muscle mass (2017)
why: Schoenfeld original weekly-set dose-response meta-analysis

title: Effect of Resistance Training Frequency on Gains in Muscular Strength (2018)
why: Grgic frequency meta-analysis; volume-equated frequency conclusion

title: Training Volume Landmarks for Muscle Growth (Renaissance Periodization)
why: Primary published definition of MV, MEV, MAV, MRV coaching model

title: What is best practice for training intensity and duration distribution in endurance athletes? (2010)
why: Seiler statement of the polarized training distribution

why: Buchheit and Laursen HIIT variable framework, cardiopulmonary emphasis

title: Aerobic high-intensity intervals improve VO2max more than moderate training (2007)

why: Thomas stretching dose-response; weekly stretch time per muscle

title: Effects of Chronic Static Stretching on Maximal Strength and Muscle Hypertrophy (2024)
why: Warneke long-duration stretching meta-analysis, full text free

title: Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function (2022)
why: Schumann updated concurrent training meta-analysis, full text free

title: ACSM Position Stand: Progression Models in Resistance Training for Healthy Adults (2009)

title: Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations Between Low- vs High-Load Resistance Training (2017)
why: Schoenfeld load-spectrum meta-analysis behind the load recommendation

why: Refalo evidence for RIR targets rather than training to failure

title: Dose-Response Between Estimated Proximity to Failure and Hypertrophy and Strength (2024)
why: Refalo meta-regression quantifying the proximity-to-failure gradient

title: The Effect of Weekly Set Volume on Strength Gain: A Meta-Analysis (2017)
why: Ralston volume-for-strength counterpart to the hypertrophy volume work

title: Effects of short versus long inter-set rest intervals in resistance training (2017)
why: Grgic rest-interval systematic review behind rest prescriptions

title: Concurrent training: a meta-analysis examining interference of aerobic and resistance exercise (2012)

title: Quantifying training intensity distribution in elite endurance athletes (2006)

title: Chronic Effects of Static Stretching Exercises on Muscle Strength and Power (2023)
why: Arntz meta-analysis on whether stretching costs strength

title: Muscle Architecture Adaptations to Static Stretching Training (2023)
why: Panidi review of structural adaptation to stretch dose

title: Physiology of Stretch-Mediated Hypertrophy and Strength Increases: A Narrative Review (2023)
why: Mechanism paper behind long-duration stretching claims

title: Dose-response associations between accelerometry measured physical activity and mortality (2019)
why: Ekelund harmonised meta-analysis, core evidence for the WHO dose

title: Effect of physical inactivity on major non-communicable diseases worldwide (2012)
why: Lee Lancet burden estimate motivating the US guideline targets
